memory_update.text: PLTR is the high-attention reference leader for defense data integration and supply-chain visibility; use it as a benchmark, not the core underfollowed discovery target.
ROP deserves underfollowed-node tracking because Deltek is a hidden GovCon compliance and workflow asset inside a large diversified vertical-software company.

SNX/DLT is a second-order public-sector secure-supply-chain and CMMC compliance channel candidate; monitor whether compliance creates margin or mix improvement rather than just pass-through distribution volume.
XMTR is a mid-cap hypothesis for supplier discovery and alternate manufacturing capacity if DoD supply-chain illumination drives demand for qualified domestic or allied supplier networks.

Many pure-play supply-chain illumination and contractor-risk vendors appear private, including Exiger, Interos, Resilinc, Everstream, Unanet, and Apptega; public exposure may therefore require parent-company, platform, reseller, or indirect workflow mapping.

FiscalNote/N﻿OTE has direct regulatory and risk-data relevance but was excluded from the main candidate list because it is a micro-cap/OTC speculative shadow after NYSE delisting; revisit only in a separate high-risk micro-cap pass.

TLS is the cleanest underfollowed public small-cap candidate for the supply-chain visibility/compliance node because Xacta explicitly maps to federal cyber GRC, CMMC, NIST 800-171, and SCRM workflows.

DSGX is a mid-cap second-order compliance-data candidate via denied-party screening, sanctions/watchlist data, export controls, and global trade compliance; verify defense/aerospace exposure and segment contribution.

XMTR belongs in the discovery lane as a contractor-onboarding/procurement-network hypothesis rather than a pure compliance-software candidate; CMMC Level 2 and government procurement positioning are the key validation hooks.

Dun & Bradstreet would have been a strong public candidate for public-sector supplier-risk data and sub-tier supply-chain illumination, but it was acquired by Clearlake and delisted in 2025; track as private benchmark only.
The node appears to split into three public-market sub-buckets: federal cyber/compliance automation, trade/sanctions/export-control screening, and supplier-network/procurement workflow platforms.
PLTR is the obvious reference anchor for defense supply-chain data platforms, but it is high-attention and mega-cap; use only as context when hunting underfollowed assets.
TLS is a plausible underfollowed CMMC/cyber-GRC compliance-gate candidate; survival in later layers requires revenue evidence that Xacta/CMMC demand is material.
DSGX is a plausible underfollowed trade-compliance/sanctions-screening candidate; verify aerospace, defense, and government-contractor customer exposure before upgrading.
BBAI is a speculative shadow candidate: defense/federal AI analytics overlap is real, but supply-chain illumination exposure must be proven through specific contracts or revenue disclosures.

Several pure-play supply-chain illumination vendors appear private, including categories like supplier mapping, contractor onboarding, and third-party risk platforms; public-market mapping may therefore rely on adjacent software/data vendors rather than pure plays.
DNB/Dun & Bradstreet had strong public-sector sub-tier supplier illumination evidence but appears to have been acquired/delisted; treat as category evidence, not an active US-listed candidate.
TENB should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a mid-cap cyber-exposure vendor with plausible CMMC and contractor cyber-posture mapping; validate via federal awards and DIB customer evidence.

FROG should remain in the Layer 1 universe as an SBOM/software-supply-chain traceability candidate; key survival test is public-sector ARR or contract evidence tied to federal software supply-chain mandates.
SNX/DLT is a hidden public-sector secure procurement channel candidate; exposure is diluted by broad IT distribution, but CMMC Level 2 and secure-supply-chain posture are directly relevant.

NOTE is a speculative shadow candidate only: direct risk-intelligence product mapping exists, but micro-cap size, liquidity, and business durability require strict verification before later-layer inclusion.

Many direct supply-chain illumination specialists identified in searches appear private, including Interos, Exiger, Black Kite, BlueVoyant, Fortress Government Solutions, and Exostar; public-market mapping may therefore be indirect through cyber platforms, SBOM vendors, federal IT distributors, and integrators.
GSA SCRIPTS BPA evidence supports the node hypothesis that supply-chain illumination is becoming a formal software/data procurement category, not just ad hoc consulting.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found that the purest public-market exposure is limited because several best-fit supply-chain illumination vendors are private. The investable map therefore splits into: 1 reference leader with obvious DoD data-platform exposure; 2 parent-company or platform names where the relevant asset is hidden inside a broader business; and 1 mid-cap marketplace that could become a second-order beneficiary if supply-chain mapping becomes tied to domestic manufacturing-network onboarding. This is research mapping only, not a trading recommendation. Layer 1B expands the public-company universe for the supply-chain visibility/compliance node. The best underfollowed fit found in this pass is Telos, because its Xacta offering maps directly to federal cyber risk, CMMC, and supply-chain risk management. Descartes is a second-order compliance-data candidate through denied-party, sanctions, export-control, and trade-compliance workflows used by aerospace/defense and supply-chain teams. Xometry is not a pure compliance-software vendor, but its marketplace, CMMC certification, government procurement positioning, and certified domestic supplier network make it relevant to contractor onboarding and capacity mapping. Palantir is included only as a high-attention reference anchor for defense data integration/readiness workflows; it should not crowd out the underfollowed lane. Layer 1B expands the universe around supply-chain visibility and compliance software for defense/government supply chains. The strongest policy signal is that DoD and primes lack visibility below tier 2 while
